candidate_relations.reason: Abundant acid-fast bacilli, high bacterial index, and storiform foamy histiocytes support histoid leprosy rather than sarcoidosis.
Leprosy is correct broadly but does not preserve the required histoid subtype.
Erythema induratum does not account for the multibacillary storiform histiocytic nodules characteristic of histoid leprosy.
Lupus pernio is a chronic cutaneous manifestation of sarcoidosis and is incompatible with the abundant acid-fast bacilli and high bacterial index.
An elevated rheumatoid factor alone does not establish rheumatoid arthritis, and the bacilli-rich histology identifies histoid leprosy.
The discrete nodules, storiform foamy histiocytes, grenz zone, abundant acid-fast bacilli, and bacterial index of 4.8 are diagnostic of histoid leprosy.
Erythema nodosum leprosum is an inflammatory reaction complicating multibacillary leprosy, not the final diagnosis represented by these chronic painless histoid nodules.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Leprosy reaction rather than the underlying histoid subtype

candidate_relations.reason: Histoid leprosy is generally regarded as a distinctive variant within the lepromatous multibacillary spectrum, so lepromatous leprosy omits the required histoid subtype.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Broader multibacillary parent classification lacking histoid morphology

candidate_relations.reason: Lupus vulgaris is cutaneous tuberculosis and typically paucibacillary, unlike the numerous bacilli and histoid architecture shown here.
Necrobiosis lipoidica does not produce abundant acid-fast bacilli or the characteristic histoid leprosy architecture.
Rheumatoid nodules show palisading granulomas around fibrinoid necrosis, not bacilli-filled storiform histiocytes; there is also no clinical rheumatoid arthritis.
Erythema nodosum presents as tender inflammatory subcutaneous nodules and does not explain the abundant acid-fast bacilli or high bacterial index.
Positive autoantibodies without corresponding systemic features do not outweigh the bacilli-rich histopathology diagnostic of histoid leprosy.
